data.title: Qnity appoints semiconductor finance veteran Ken Rizvi as CFO
data.description:
• Qnity Electronics (Q) appointed semiconductor finance veteran Ken Rizvi as senior vice president and chief financial officer, effective October 1.
  • He will succeed Michael Goss, who has served as interim CFO. While, Goss will become Qnity’s vice president of finance and controllership.
  • Ken brings more than 25 years of financial experience, including extensive CFO and senior finance roles across the semiconductor ecosystem. He most recently served as CFO of Synaptics (SYNA), where he oversaw global finance, corporate development, investor relations and IT.

data.title: Wynn Resorts faces a potential employee strike at its Boston property
data.description:
Wynn Resorts' (WYNN) Encore Boston Harbor casino and hotel property in Everett, Massachusetts, is facing the prospect of a labor strike. More than 1,300 unionized workers voted this week to authorize a strike as negotiations over a new labor agreement stalled ahead of the August 31 expiration of their current contract.

The workforce includes hotel and food-service employees such as housekeepers, cooks, servers, bartenders, cleaners, dishwashers, drivers, cocktail servers, bar porters, and slot attendants. The workers are represented primarily by the Unite Here Local 26 and Teamsters Local 25 unions.

Workers want a new contract that improves compensation and protects benefits. Union priorities include a $10 wage increase over four years, continued benefits, and pension protections for longer-serving employees. Union leaders have argued that Encore Boston Harbor has the financial capacity to meet those demands, pointing to approximately $847M in revenue at the resort last year. 

The strike authorization vote does not itself create a strike or set a guaranteed walkout date. However, it permits the union membership and leadership to call one if negotiations fail. If Wynn Resorts and the unions do not reach a settlement or agree to extend the existing agreement, a strike could begin as soon as August 31.

data.title: BJ's Wholesale gains after comparable sales and membership fee income shine in Q2
data.description:
BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings (BJ) gained in early action on Friday after the warehouse club chain released a strong second-quarter earnings report.

Total comparable club sales shot up 11.9% during the quarter. Excluding the impact of gasoline sales, comparable club sales were up 3.1%. Top-line revenue of $6.23B beat the consensus estimate by $290M.

Membership fee income increased 9.9% year-over-year to $135.6M in the second quarter. The increase was primarily driven by strength in membership acquisition, retention, and higher-tier membership penetration across both new and existing clubs. On a smaller scale, the membership fee income growth was stronger than the recent paces for Costco (COST) and Sam's Club (WMT).

The merchandise gross margin rate, which excludes gasoline sales and membership fee income, decreased by approximately 20 basis points compared to a year ago, primarily driven by the company’s continued investments in pricing, partially offset by tariff refund benefits recognized

Adjusted EBITDA increased by 14.3% to $347.2M. Non-GAAP EPS was reported at $1.36 vs. $1.17 consensus and $1.14 a year ago.

"We delivered a strong second quarter, coming in ahead of our expectations across sales and profitability, with strong membership momentum. Our value proposition continued to resonate with members in our clubs and at our gas stations, and the momentum we're seeing across our strategic priorities gives us real confidence in the road ahead," stated CEO Bob Eddy.

Looking ahead, BJ's (BJ) sees comparable club sales, excluding the impact of gasoline sales, increasing 2.0% to 3.0% year-over-year for the full year. Adjusted EPS is seen landing in a range from $4.60 to $4.80 (midpoint $4.70) vs. the consensus estimate of $4.53.

Shares of BJ's (BJ) rose 1.2% in premarket trading to $92.36 vs. the 52-week range of $83.21 to $105.78.

data.title: Synaptics CFO Ken Rizvi resigns
data.description:
Synaptics (SYNA) said Ken Rizvi has resigned from his position as chief financial officer, effective immediately, to pursue another opportunity.

Rizvi will remain employed in an advisory role through September 30, 2026 to assist with the transition of his responsibilities.

The firm has elected not to conduct a search at this time for a successor CFO due to the announcement on June 25, 2026 of the pending merger between Synaptics and onsemi.

Rahul Patel, president and CEO, will serve as the principal financial officer through the closing of the merger.

Kermit Nolan, Synaptics' former chief accounting officer, is returning as a consultant to advise the internal team through the transition. Over his 20-year tenure, he held several roles at the company, including acting CFO.

data.title: Take-Two, Meta lead communication services growth rankings as telecom giants lag
data.description:
As we navigate the third quarter of 2026, the S&P Communication Services sector (XLC) continues to experience significant macroeconomic headwinds and shifting demand dynamics, making strategic stock selection and growth assessments a primary focus for active market participants.

Below is a list of the top holdings of the S&P Communication Services sector arranged according to their growth grade. These specific companies are selected because they represent the largest, most influential holdings in the sector by market capitalization, offering a comprehensive look at how the sector's heavyweights are scaling and expanding. Any grade of B- or above is considered a Buy, while a grade of D+ or below is considered a Sell.

The list is topped by Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO), with a growth grade of A. Meta Platforms (META) follows with a B grade, while T-Mobile US (TMUS) earns a B-, making these three stocks the only ones in the Buy category.

The remaining holdings fall into Hold or Sell territory, with Alphabet (GOOG) holding a C+ grade and The Walt Disney Company (DIS) earning a C. AT&T (T), Verizon Communications (VZ), and Comcast Corporation (CMCSA) round out the bottom of the list with grades of D, D-, and F respectively.

The growth factor grade is a quantitative assessment used in stock analysis to evaluate a company's growth prospects and expansion trajectory. This metric systematically analyzes multiple growth-related indicators to determine how effectively a company is scaling its business operations.

Growth factor grades are typically expressed on a letter scale (A+ through F), where higher grades indicate stronger growth characteristics relative to sector peers. An A+ grade represents exceptional growth potential, while lower grades suggest more moderate expansion or potential headwinds.

data.title: These stocks could benefit from the new English Premier League season
data.description:
The 2026-27 Premier League begins on Friday with Arsenal playing Coventry City. The season runs until May 30, with 380 fixtures. 

It is the second year of the league's four-year domestic media rights cycle, worth a record £6.7B across the 2025-2026 to 2028-2029. Sky carries the bulk of live inventory, while TNT Sports (WBD) has a 52-match package in the UK. Comcast (CMCSA) holds the broadcast and streaming rights in the U.S. through NBC, USA Network, and Peacock, which will carry all 380 matches this season. The popularity of the English Premier League in the U.S. helps support Peacock engagement, advertising demand, and subscriber retention for Comcast (CMCSA). 

Nike (NKE), Adidas (ADDYY), Puma (PMMAF), and Fanatics (FANA) are some main beneficiaries of the EPL on the apparel and footwear side of the business. Puma (PMMAF) has the league-wide role as official ball partner, while Adidas (ADDYY) has strong club relationships with high-profile teams Arsenal and Manchester United (MANU), creating especially visible exposure around high-profile fixtures and European competition. Front-of-short sponsors include Emirates (Arsenal), AIA (Tottenham), and Leeds United (Red Bull). Microsoft (MSFT), Adobe (ADBE), Barclays (BCS), and Electronic Arts are other official EPL partners.

Flutter Entertainment (FLUT), Entain (GMVHF), bet365, and Evoke (EIHDF) are the sports betting companies with the highest percentage of their revenue tied to English football.

Manchester United (MANU) is the closest thing to a pure play stock bet on the Premier League, as it supports broadcast income and matchday revenue for the company. The club's placement in the EPL is crucial in determining if it plays in the lucrative Champions League the following season.
